PUBLIC COMMENT RULES

“(California Government Code Section 54954.3).
(a) Every agenda for a special meeting shall provide an opportunity for members of the
public to directly address the legislative body on any item that has been described in the
notice for the meeting, before or during the legislative body’s consideration of the item,
that is within the subject matter jurisdiction of the legislative body, provided that no action
shall be taken on any item not appearing on the agenda unless the action is otherwise
authorized by subdivision (b) of Section 54954.2 [section omitted].

(b) (1) The legislative body of a local agency may adopt reasonable regulations to ensure
that the intent of the subdivision (a) is carried out, including, but not limited to, regulations
limiting the total amount of time allocated for public testimony on particular issues and for
each individual speaker.
  (2) Notwithstanding paragraph (1), when the legislative body of a local agency limits
time for public comment, the legislative body of a local agency shall provide at least twice

ENVIRONMENTAL REVIEW

Pursuant to the California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA), City staff determined the
project to be Categorically Exempt from environmental proceedings pursuant to Section
15315, Minor Land Divisions, which exempts the division of property in urbanized areas
zoned for residential, commercial, or industrial use into four or fewer parcels. The project
qualifies for this exemption because the request to subdivide is less than four parcels and
the subject site is relatively flat. In addition, no development is proposed as part of this
application.

  WHEREAS, Shaughne S. Warnack Trust has filed an application requesting the
approval of Tentative Parcel Map (TPM) 84606, described herein (hereinafter referred to
as “Application”); and

  WHEREAS, The Application applies to one existing parcel totaling approximately
13.77 acres located on the northwest corner of Rancho Vista Boulevard and Division
Street as indicated on the Los Angeles County Assessor roll as Assessor Parcel Number
3005-004-060, legally described in Exhibit A hereto and shown on the map attached as
Exhibit B; and

  WHEREAS, On March 13, 2025, the Planning Commission of the City of Palmdale
conducted a duly noticed public hearing on the Application and concluded said hearing
on that date.

NOW THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED, THE PLANNING COMMISSION OF THE CITY
OF PALMDALE DOES HEREBY FIND, DETERMINE, RESOLVE AND ORDER AS
FOLLOWS:

  SECTION 1. The Planning Commission hereby specifically finds that all of the facts
set forth in the Recitals of the Resolution are true and correct.

  SECTION 2. The Planning Commission hereby finds as follows with respect to the
environmental documentation prepared for the Application:

  A  The proposed project is categorically exempt from environmental
  proceedings pursuant to Section 15315, Minor Land Divisions, of the
  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Guidelines, which exempts
  the division of property in urbanized areas zoned for residential,
  commercial, or industrial use into four or fewer parcels. The project qualifies
  for this exemption because the request to subdivide is less than four parcels
  and the subject site is relatively flat. In addition, no development is proposed
  as part of this application.

  B  The custodian of records for the environmental document, and all other
  materials which constitute the record of proceedings upon which the

  City of Palmdale. These documents are available for public review in the
  Planning Division of the City of Palmdale located at 38250 Sierra Highway,

  SECTION 3. Based upon substantial evidence presented to this Commission
during the March 13, 2025, public hearing, including public testimony and written and oral
staff reports, this Commission specifically finds as follows:

  A  The proposed subdivision, together with the provisions for its design and
  improvement, is consistent and compatible with the maps, goals, objectives,
  and policies of the General Plan and the Palmdale Municipal Code.

  The proposed subdivision as discussed in Exhibit C, meets the goals,
  objectives, and policies of the General Plan, because the two parcels will
  allow for a variety of development at this location. In addition, the proposed
  subdivision as discussed in Exhibit D, meets the minimum lot width and lot
  depth dimensions required of the Neighborhood Commercial (NC) zone, of
  the Palmdale Municipal Code.

  B  The tentative map does not propose to divide land which is subject to
  contract entered into pursuant to the California Land Conservation Act of
  1965.

  A review of the preliminary title report for the subject property revealed that
  the property in question has not been included in any such contract.

  C  The site is physically suitable for the type and proposed density of
  development proposed by the tentative map.

  The site is capable of supporting development because Parcel 1 will be
  approximately 6.89 acres and Parcel 2 will be approximately 6.58 acres
  which are large enough to reasonably accommodate future development.
  Parcel 1 has the potential to provide access either from Rancho Vista
  Boulevard, Division Street, or both, and Parcel 2 has the potential to
  provide access from Division Street. As proposed, the subdivision does not
  include any physical changes to the site. The applicant will be required to
  record a reciprocal access, parking, maintenance, sewer, and drainage
  agreement as part of the TPM. This is required so that when future
  development is proposed, both parcels will be required to share and
  maintain on-site facilities.

  D  The design of the subdivision and the proposed improvements are not likely
  to cause substantial environmental damage or substantially and avoidably
  injure fish or wildlife or their habitat.

  E  The design of the subdivision and the type of improvements are not likely
  to cause serious public health and safety problems.

  F  The tentative map design provides for future passive or natural heating or
  cooling opportunities in the subdivision to the extent feasible.

  G  The design of the subdivision and the type of improvements will not conflict
  with easements acquired by the public at large for access through or use of
  the private property within the proposed subdivision, or the design of the
  subdivision and the type of improvements will conflict with the easements
  acquired by the public at large for access through or use of property within
  the proposed subdivision but alternate easements which are substantially
  equivalent to those previously acquired by the public will be provided.

  H  The proposed subdivision represents orderly development of the project
  site and surrounding area.

  The request is for the subdivision of a vacant 13.77 parcel and no
  development is proposed at this time. As proposed, the subdivision would
  not cause substantial environmental damage. In addition, there are no
  physical changes to the site as part of the proposed subdivision. Therefore,
  it will not cause serious public health or safety problems. Future
  development of the site will be required to provide on and off-site
  improvements necessary to serve the project. When a project is proposed,
  it will be evaluated to ensure compliance for future passive and natural
  heating and cooling opportunities. The design of the subdivision will not
  conflict with any easements because all easements on the site are existing
  and will not be altered by the TPM. The applicant has depicted existing
  easements for utility and access; however, none will be intersected by the
  subdivision. The applicant is required to record a reciprocal access,
  parking, maintenance, sewer, and drainage agreement as part of the TPM,
  to ensure both parcels share and maintain on-site facilities. Lastly, when a
  project is proposed, the project will be evaluated to ensure that the
  development of the project is orderly in the surrounding area. Therefore,
  the proposed subdivision is consistent with findings D through H.

ANALYSIS

The applicant is requesting to establish a smoke shop located at 39904 10th Street West,
Suite A, within a vacant 1,575-square-foot commercial tenant space. The subject site is
within the Regional Commercial (RC) General Plan Land Use designation and zone, and
the proposed use is permissible, subject to the approval of a CUP application.

Approximately 359 square feet of total floor area will be dedicated to merchandise display
cases of tobacco products, and a total of 200 square feet will be dedicated to incense,
snacks, shirts, gifts, and accessories. The remaining area is dedicated to hallways,
spacing between display cases, office area, restroom, storage and drink coolers for non-
alcoholic beverages. The applicant is proposing to sell tobacco/smoking products and
paraphernalia from behind the counters and within display cases, out of reach from
customers. The proposed project does not include any expansion to the existing building
or modifications to the exterior of the building. Any proposed interior tenant improvements
will be reviewed through a separate tenant improvement application.

In addition, the project complies with the distance requirement for sensitive uses listed
within the Palmdale Municipal Code (PMC) for tobacco/smoking products retailers
because there are no sensitive uses located within 1,000 feet of the proposed business.

CUP 24-0016 is a request to establish a smoke shop within an existing 1,575-square-foot
commercial tenant space. This use is permitted with the approval of a CUP application.
Draft Conditions of Approval have been included to mitigate potential impacts associated
with smoke shops as required by the PMC, such as complying with local, State, and
Federal laws with advertising, display, and sale of tobacco/smoking products, operational
standards and requirements, loitering, littering, and safety.

Calls for Service

The Los Angeles County Sheriff’s Department provided a summary of service calls and
crime history for the project site between January 1, 2024, to December 17, 2024, and
the report indicates there were 42 calls for service within the entire shopping center. The
majority of the calls for service were for public disturbances by transient individuals with
a few regarding theft. After review of past service calls near the subject property, the
Los Angeles County Sheriff’s Department has not indicated any opposition to the
approval of this CUP because all calls were routine in nature and were not associated
with the proposed business. In addition, as specified within the draft Conditions of
Approval, if the proposed business generates an increase in the number of calls for
service, the Sheriff’s Department may request a subsequent review of the CUP by the
Planning Commission.

Operations

The proposed smoke shop will operate from 7 a.m. to 11 p.m. daily and have two
employees each shift. In addition, draft Conditions of Approval have been included to
ensure that all merchandise is located within display cases or behind counters, allowing
only store employees to have immediate access to tobacco and smoking products and
paraphernalia. In addition, all store employees will be required to attend a responsible
tobacco retailer training program. Lastly, the applicant will install security cameras inside
and outside the establishment.

ENVIRONMENTAL REVIEW

The proposed project is categorically exempt from California Environmental Quality Act
(CEQA) Guidelines review pursuant to Section 15301, Class 1, Existing Facilities of the
CEQA Guidelines, which exempts the operation, permitting, and licensing involving
negligible or no expansion of existing or former use. The proposed smoke shop within an
existing building does not include any expansion of the existing building. Therefore, the
project is exempt per CEQA Section 15301, Class 1 Existing Facilities.

BACKGROUND

The existing 720-square-foot convenience market and three-island fueling station was
approved by Los Angeles County in 1955. In 1962 the City of Palmdale incorporated, and
following the City’s incorporation, permits were obtained in 1964 to expand the building.
This expansion included a lubrication room to the southern back wall of the building
measuring 154 square feet and a pump island canopy of 1,800 square feet. Permits for
the lubrication room and pump island canopy were finalized on March 9, 1965; however,
it was later found that the lubrication room was constructed larger than approved and
measured approximately 176 square feet, giving the convenience market and fueling
station a building footprint of 896 square feet.

Sometime after 1965, an unpermitted upgrade to the entryway was made to the exterior
façade of the building, increasing its footprint from 896 square feet to the current building
size of 908 square feet. Therefore, according to the building permit records obtained from
Los Angeles County, the building should be 874 square feet, and 34 square feet is
unpermitted.

Currently, the existing commercial building, known as Kwik Serv Market, is located in the

operational 24/7. According to the Palmdale Transit Area Specific Plan (PTASP) Figure

  The proposed improvements may enhance the physical aspects of the
  property; however, they do not directly address the preservation of
  substantial rights related to its non-conforming land use. The fueling station,
  classified as a non-permitted use, significantly limits the property's ability to
  enjoy the same rights and privileges as other properties in the area. While
  the proposal includes landscaping, parking, and other amenities, these
  changes do not resolve the fundamental issue of the non-permitted land
  use. This ongoing limitation could still hinder the property's potential
  compared to those with conforming uses.

  C  The application will not be materially detrimental to the public health, safety,
  or welfare, or injurious to the properties or improvements in the vicinity and
  under the same zone in which the property is located, and; (VAR)

  D  The application does not constitute a special privilege inconsistent with the
  limitations upon other properties in the vicinity and in the same zone in
  which the property is located. (VAR)

  The proposed improvements to the existing site will grant the property
  special privileges by allowing significant modifications and enhancements,
  including façade changes, landscaping improvements, and the addition of
  new parking areas, all while the non-permitted fueling station remains in
  place. These changes clearly provide the property with an unfair advantage
  over conforming properties in the same zone, which are bound by stricter
  regulations. The combination of the non-conforming use (the fueling station)
  and these enhancements will enable the property to operate in a manner
  that contradicts the limitations placed on other properties. This situation
  creates a special privilege that surrounding properties do not receive,
  undermining fairness within the community.

  E  That the proposed use is consistent with the goals, policies, and objectives
  of the General Plan and the purposes of the zone in which the project is
  located. (MSPR)

  F  The proposed project meets all applicable standards of this Title including,
  but not limited to, setbacks, height, separations, wall, fence, lighting, and
  landscaping standards. (MSPR)

  G  That the proposed project, together with the conditions applicable thereto,
  will not be detrimental to the public health, safety, or welfare or materially
  injurious to properties or improvements in the vicinity. (MSPR)

  The project involves expanding a 908-square-foot legal non-conforming
  commercial building by an additional 144 square feet along with various
  onsite improvements and modifications to the existing exterior. The project
  is not consistent with the policies and objectives of the General Plan and
  the applicable standards of Title 17, as shown in Exhibits C and D. In
  addition, this proposed expansion id not permissible and does not align with
  the goals and long-term vision of the Palmdale Transit Area Specific Plan
  (PTASP).

  The current auto-oriented use of the site discourages pedestrian activity.
  Expanding the building while maintaining this auto-centric approach could
  conflict with these goals and hinder progress toward the City’s long-term
  vision for the area. This inconsistency with the General Plan’s objectives,
  such as promoting active streetscapes, improving transportation options,
  and fostering a more integrated, livable community, highlights why the
  proposed expansion would be detrimental to public health, safety, and
  welfare, and could also have a materially injurious impact on the
  surrounding properties and the community as a whole.
